correctness.rationale: Orthogonality gives N^(-2) times the incidence form. For each h and kernel coset A the actual Cauchy bound for (2)–(3) is |sum_A f(x+h) conjugate(f(x))|^2 <= (sum_A |f(x+h)|^2)(sum_A |f(x)|^2); expanding the product yields M(d) because 2h(d-h)=0. It is not the bound on the sequence of products against a constant sequence. Thus the proposed concern about product constancy does not apply: equality gives proportionality of the two vectors, including their zero entries. The congruence count follows by splitting the valuation of h below, equal to, or above that of d below k, and by requiring h divisible by 2^k for d divisible by 2^k. The mass bound forces one parent coset with two equal positive daughter masses. At h=2^k its kernel is the parent subgroup and the two vectors have the same nonzero norm. Their proportionality gives one unit eigenvalue of order dividing 2^k, hence one shared character on the two daughters. Conversely the packets give proportional vectors for h in the daughter subgroup on all cosets (zero outside the parent); for parent-only shifts the daughters swap and each kernel coset has its own constant multiplier. Other shifts have disjoint supports. The projective count follows from disjoint support labels and distinct eigenvalues; each free relative phase is an embedded circle, including k=1. The frozen finite tests are corroboration, not the quantified proof.
